paper.title_en: Phenomenological search for light neutral scalar couplings in elastic electron-proton scattering within a two-photon-exchange-consistent framework
paper.abstract_en: In this work, a comprehensive, two-photon-exchange (TPE)-consistent analysis of the unpolarized reduced cross section <math><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>ɛ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> for elastic electron-proton (<math><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>) scattering is performed to search for possible contributions from a light neutral scalar mediator and to establish quantitative constraints in their absence. The framework incorporates the standard one-photon-exchange (OPE) term, the phenomenological TPE correction, and an additional scalar amplitude whose strength is governed by the dimensionless coupling ratio <math><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math>, defined as the scalar proton-electron coupling <math><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></math> normalized to the electromagnetic fine-structure constant <math><mi>α</mi></math>. The scalar strength <math><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> is extracted from linear Rosenbluth fits to world <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></math> data at 134 <math><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> points spanning <math><mrow><mn>0.0155</mn><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≤</mo><mn>5.5</mn><mspace width="4pt"/><msup><mi>GeV</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>. The data exhibit no statistically significant deviation from the <math><mrow><mi>OPE</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>TPE</mi></mrow></math> baseline, and the global profile likelihood saturates the physical boundary <math><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>̂</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> for all scanned mediator masses. One-sided 95% confidence-level upper limits <math><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>95</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> are obtained using a profile-likelihood construction over the mass range <math><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>10</mn><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>GeV</mi></mrow></math>. Accordingly, the primary result of this work is the determination of quantitative exclusion limits on the scalar coupling, rather than evidence of a nonzero contribution. The resulting exclusion curve lies at the level of a few <math><mrow><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> to <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> depending on <math><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></math>, with systematic uncertainties increasing the limits by only 5–10% across most of the mass range. These limits improve upon, or are comparable to, previously reported electromagnetic-form-factor-based scalar constraints in the low- to intermediate-mass region and constitute the first dedicated, TPE-consistent <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></math>-based search for light scalar exchange in elastic <math><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> scattering. No evidence for a scalar contribution is observed within the present experimental sensitivity.
